newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram urges states to introduce VAT.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram urges states to introduce VAT.

text.p: Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Friday urged India's state governments to adopt value-added tax (VAT) systems as soon as possible to promote trade.

"It would be desirable that all states should move over to VAT at the earliest time after making sufficient preparation," a Finance Ministry statement quoted Chidambaram as telling state finance ministers.
State finance ministers in their last meeting in December 1995 had broadly agreed on the phased introduction of a VAT system.
But Chidambaram said only some Indian states had introduced the VAT while others needed to follow the lead.
The finance minister said the central sales tax had emerged as a significant component of states' sales tax revenue but that it had its pitfalls.

"Often it becomes a source of economic distortion and inhibits the growth of a large common market," he said. "(It) also leads to cascading with consequent burden on industry and exports causing distortion in location of industry."
Chidambaram warned against overuse of stamp duties.
He said "a high level of incidence of stamp duty retards economic growth and reduces long-term buoyancy of revenue besides causing duty avoidance and evasion".
It added that different duty rates among states can distort economic activity and cause a loss of revenue to some states.
Chidambaram said basic structural reforms were needed to improve the efficiency and profitability of state enterprises.

In their meeting in 1995, the finance ministers of states had also agreed to set up a group to examine the phasing out of inter-state sales tax and take steps needed to transform India into a common market without affecting states' revenues.
"There still exists wide disparity in rates; states are still competing with each other to attract trade and industry," the statement said.
